Standard: Solid rocket motors are qualified for carriage and operation in the air vehicle flight environment during all operating conditions and do not fail prematurely (deflagrate, rupture, or explode) due to overpressure or design deficiencies while in proximity to the air vehicle. For unqualified rocket motors, if the potential for overpressure failure or deflagration of solid rocket motors exists, mitigations are established to ensure safe separation distance between the air vehicle and the rocket motor prior to ignition. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine design documentation for the rocket motor ignition system and firing sequence to determine the minimum time and distance between store release and rocket motor ignition.
(2) Examine design documentation to identify potential failure modes in the ignition system. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct rocket motor overpressure SEA by modeling the air vehicle, rocket motor, and fragment trajectories that include the time of predicted failure. rocket motor overpressure SEA assumes that the rocket motor deflagrates or ruptures at rocket motor ignition unless there is credible data verifying time of rupture as demonstrated through modeling or during static fire testing. Ph to the air vehicle or Pk by fragmentation modeling considers factors such as the air vehicle release conditions and flight path, the weapon’s trajectory and orientation after launch, and the rocket motor fragmentation characteristics data due to rocket motor overpressure or deflagration. Rocket motor fragmentation may be informed by design data, modeling, or static arena testing. If available, rocket motor failure/reliability can be taken into consideration as part of the overarching Ph and Pk calculation.
  (2) Evaluate the Ph from a rocket motor fragment that could impact the air vehicle.
  (3) Evaluate the Pk from fragmentation. Probability of kill calculation should include modeling the vulnerable areas of the launch air vehicle obtained from vulnerability analyses.
  (4) Evaluate mitigations that ensure safe separation distance between the air vehicle and rocket motor ignition point (e.g., delayed rocket motor ignition, safe escape maneuver).
  (5) Identify the set of flight conditions (altitude, speed and engagement range) that will provide the air vehicle protection from the munition deflagration in the event of rocket motor failure. This set of flight conditions, at a minimum, should include the planned flight test and release points as part of the live fire testing. Ideally, the data set should characterize the entire employment envelope and weapon flight modes and rocket motor ignition times. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Complete rocket motor qualification testing IAW NAVSEAINST 8020.5 to include static firing of rocket motors with no anomalies that could allude to premature rocket motor failure prior to developmental test use. Provide demonstration of rocket motor reliability, specifically failure rate, through the rocket motor ignition and burn phase. Static fire test data will inform the SEA. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Complete rocket motor qualification testing to include static firing of rocket motors with no anomalies that could allude to premature rocket motor failure prior to operational use and fielding. Provide demonstration of rocket motor reliability, specifically failure rate, through the full phase of flight to termination.
